text:
UN General Assembly resolutions are a material source of international law: they may enunciate statements of customary law, but they do not always reflect it. They are not a formal source under Article 38 of the ICJ Statute, and outside Charter matters such as the budget they are recommendatory. Their weight depends on support, normative wording, and consistency with state practice, which can show opinio juris or later harden into custom.
